system_title: National Virtual Courts Traffic Challan Redressal System
statutory_basis: Section 208 MVA 1988 (Summary disposal of cases); Section 206 CrPC / Section 231 BNSS

general_guidelines.escalation_stage: Regular Metropolitan Magistrate / Chief Judicial Magistrate Court
general_guidelines.evidence_standard: CMVR Rule 167A (Mandatory photographic/video proof with timestamp and geo-coordinates)
general_guidelines.statutory_appeal: High Court under Section 397/401 CrPC or Section 438 BNSS

Delhi.contest_transfer_court: Metropolitan Magistrate (Traffic) Court of concerned police district
Delhi.special_notes: Delhi processes 100% of camera-captured notices (speed, red light, bus lane) through Virtual Courts. Unpaid challans after 90 days are automatically escalated for physical summons.

Maharashtra.contest_transfer_court: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) / Special Metropolitan Magistrate
Maharashtra.special_notes: Mumbai and Pune traffic police notices are routed through e-Challan payment gateway and Virtual Court.

Uttar Pradesh.virtual_court_name: UP Virtual Traffic Court (Lucknow, Noida, Ghaziabad, Kanpur)
Uttar Pradesh.special_notes: Summons window is strictly 60 days before file is placed before physical court for issuing bailable warrants.

Karnataka.special_notes: Karnataka allows both online plea and offline compounding at Karnataka One / Traffic Police Stations.

Tamil Nadu.special_notes: Integrated with Greater Chennai Traffic Police (GCTP) e-Challan enforcement.

Kerala.special_notes: AI camera challans from Safe Kerala Project are adjudicated under this court.

Gujarat.special_notes: Covers One Nation One Challan project notices for major municipal commissionerates.

Haryana.special_notes: Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) camera challans are processed here.

West Bengal.special_notes: Kolkata Police Automated CCTV Challan System notices are listed here.

Odisha.special_notes: Statewide camera e-challan enforcement integrated with e-Courts.

Punjab.special_notes: Enforcement notices on national highways and city roads.

Andhra Pradesh.contest_transfer_court: Special Judicial Magistrate of Second Class
Andhra Pradesh.special_notes: Integrated with AP Police e-Challan and Parivahan.

grounds_to_contest.name: Defective Photographic Proof — Registration Plate Illegible
grounds_to_contest.recommendation: Contest challan before Magistrate. CMVR Rule 167A mandates clear photographic proof showing registration plate.

grounds_to_contest.name: Mismatched Vehicle Type or Class
grounds_to_contest.statutory_basis: Section 136A MVA 1988; Parivahan Vahan Master Record
grounds_to_contest.recommendation: Contest immediately. Provide RC copy showing vehicle class differs from the camera recognition record.

grounds_to_contest.name: Expired Radar / Camera Calibration Certificate
grounds_to_contest.recommendation: Contest and file RTI request under Sec 6(1) for calibration certificate. Speed radar readings without valid calibration are inadmissible.

grounds_to_contest.name: Giving Way to Emergency Vehicle (Ambulance / Fire Brigade)
grounds_to_contest.statutory_basis: Section 194E MVA 1988; Rule 115 Rules of the Road
grounds_to_contest.recommendation: Contest in court. Yielding to an emergency vehicle is a mandatory statutory duty under Sec 194E; crossing stop line for this purpose is legally protected.

grounds_to_contest.name: Vehicle Stolen or Already Transferred Prior to Incident
grounds_to_contest.statutory_basis: Section 50 MVA (Transfer of ownership); Section 379 IPC / Section 303 BNS
grounds_to_contest.recommendation: Submit FIR copy of vehicle theft or Form 29/30 sale delivery receipt. Registered owner is immune if vehicle was stolen or transferred.
